## Highlights

- `wclass run` and `wclass route` require you to say where the tier comes from: exactly one of
  `--tier` (you choose) or `--suggest-tier` (the local classifier suggests, and prints its own
  measured record next to the suggestion). The refuted heuristic classifier is no longer the
  default front door, and a suggested tier cannot start a vendor without a review.
- When stdout is a terminal, `wclass run` shows the task-free route on the controlling terminal
  and asks before starting it. No copied fingerprint is needed there. `--no-review`, an explicit
  `--json` before the command, or `--ack-route-fingerprint` selects the non-interactive path, and a
  pipe never gains a prompt.
- Every `run` and `route` flag now has help text. `--source-vendor` and the tier selection lead
  the usage line, and each `--help` ends with a first command to try.
- `wclass --help` lists the seven daily commands and names the seven advanced ones in one line.
  `profile`, `select`, `review-cost-profile`, `recommend`, `render`, `delegate`, and `v2` still
  parse, run, and answer their own `--help`; they are only absent from the listing.
- The packaged presets are now `<vendor>-model-override`, which is what they do: bind opaque model
  and effort labels onto the built-in route shapes. The old `<vendor>-cost-focused` names claimed
  a saving nothing here has measured. They remain accepted as aliases everywhere a preset is
  selected, and the policy files, command bytes, and fingerprints are unchanged.
- The README leads with what the tool does, then Install, Quick start, and "What you get, and what
  you do not". The measured classifier record and the paired token study were moved, not removed:
  see "Why the classifier is opt-in" and "Measured results for tier routing".

## Core routing

- The tier requirement is an argparse mutually exclusive group, so it fails before the task is
  read, and the diagnostic stays the closed `invalid_input` object. The usage line is where the
  requirement is discoverable, and a test pins that.
- `--suggest-tier` carries `CLASSIFIER_MEASURED_AGREEMENT` in the receipt and in the console
  review: agreement 10/24 (41.7%), high-tier recall 1/9 (11.1%), over-routing 6/24 (25.0%), and
  under-routing 8/9. An explicit tier adds no receipt field, so the frozen schema-1 route bytes are
  unchanged and no fingerprint moved.
- The terminal review default is keyed to one signal: stdout is a terminal. An explicit `--human`
  in a pipe does not open a prompt; an explicit `--json` on a terminal does not either. `--review`
  and `--no-review` together are rejected rather than resolved in one direction. A pty-backed
  harness looks like a terminal, so give it `--no-review` or a fingerprint.
- `review-preset` and `route` receipts report the canonical preset name in their `preset` field. A
  script that compares that field to an old `-cost-focused` string needs the new one; nothing else
  about the receipt changed.
- `docs/integrations.md` examples that ran `route`/`run` without a tier source were fixed, and a
  test now scans every shell block in every markdown file for that defect.

## Guidance and documentation

- Project guidance is split by directory scope. The root `AGENTS.md` carries shared rules and an
  index; `src/weightclass/AGENTS.md`, `src/weightclass/advisory/AGENTS.md`, `tests/AGENTS.md`,
  `.weightclass/AGENTS.md`, and `packaging/AGENTS.md` are authoritative inside their subtrees.
- `HANDOFF.md` records the direction research done with external reviewers, what survived
  checking and what did not, and the usability batch above.

## Compatibility and safety

**Breaking change — `run` and `route` require a tier source.** An invocation without `--tier` or
`--suggest-tier` now exits `2` with `{"error": "invalid_input"}` instead of classifying silently.
Automation should pass `--tier`; interactive use can pass `--suggest-tier` and review.

**Breaking change — terminal runs review by default.** A `wclass run` whose stdout is a terminal
now asks on the controlling terminal before starting a vendor, including for built-in routes that
previously started directly. Scripts driven through a pty should pass `--no-review` or
`--ack-route-fingerprint`. Non-terminal behaviour, including the fingerprint requirement for policy
runs, is unchanged.

**Breaking change — `preset` receipt field.** The `preset` field in `route` and `review-preset`
output carries the `<vendor>-model-override` name even when an alias selected the preset.

The one-foreground-child contract, the credential, network, and task-persistence boundaries, the
advisory companion, campaign records, statistical gates, sealed manifests, and every route
fingerprint are unchanged. The core native `agy` and `grok` routes still deliver the task in argv;
that boundary is unchanged and still documented in `src/weightclass/AGENTS.md`. The packaged
advisory Skill bundle is byte-identical to 0.30.0, so no upgrade-ledger entry was needed.

## Not in this release

Cheap-first execution with automatic escalation, the only lever the repository has measured as
large, remains unimplemented. It conflicts with the one-foreground-child contract and is a separate
decision, recorded in `HANDOFF.md`.
